e-4701.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
e-4701.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/49df59f984403cbbc994361c96313eca4d0875a7030dd997c90f1e393e23b69c.png)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
e-4701.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/dded05f0961034de6808d8f91f64afe8c367cec3c11fafdb26946090fa9c0891.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=2$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+(2)=-2\,⟹\,y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-4$ and $z=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-4)+(2)=1\,⟹\,x=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-5,$ $y=-4,$ and $z=2.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -5,-4,2 \rangle.$

e-4702.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
e-4702.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/0c3483f97994da22dc0c739f9c3a26f87e070d28b684e63955a1129d00f9c755.png)

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
e-4702.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/9f1beb75e17aabdbeb5d814ae7ce3018f2ea89c36211070d40060d57445ca936.png)

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get $a_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/84de3f5eddf0a05d4f2d69aebd1537feb23a228fba3e1af31678dd4bdb1b59df.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z,$ and the second equation $y=3$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting these values into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(3)+(1)=-2\,⟹\,x=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-6,$ $y=3,$ and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -6,3,1 \rangle.$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[101401−1−450621]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[101401−1−40012]
b
M∼[101401−1−40011]
c
M∼[101401−1−40010]
d
M∼[101401−1−4001−1]
e
M∼[101401−1−4001−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₃ ← R₃ − 5R₁. The third row becomes [0, 0, 1, 21 − 20] = [0, 0, 1, 1], giving row echelon form as in option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=0 \\  & y+2z=0 \\  & x+y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=0 \\  & y+2z=0 \\  & x+y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[134−6279−1341217−26]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[134−6011−10012]
b
M∼[134−6011−1001−1]
c
M∼[134−6011−10011]
d
M∼[134−6011−10010]
e
M∼[134−6011−1001−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − 4R₁. These give [0, 1, 1, −1] and [0, 0, 1, −2], respectively. The resulting row echelon form matches option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 7 & 9 & -13 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 7 & 9 & -13 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 12 & 17 & -26\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[134−6279−1341217−26]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[134−6011−10012]
b
M∼[134−6011−1001−1]
c
M∼[134−6011−10011]
d
M∼[134−6011−10010]
e
M∼[134−6011−1001−2]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[134−6279−1341217−26]R2:=R2−2R1∼[134−6011−141217−26]R3:=R3−4R1∼[134−6011−1001−2].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. R₂ − 2R₁ = [0, 1, 1, −1] and R₃ − 4R₁ = [0, 0, 1, −2], since −26 − 4(−6) = −2. These rows give row echelon form.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & 2x+3y+2z=14\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=3$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(3)=5\,⟹\,y=5-3=2.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=2$ and $z=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(2)+(3)=6\,⟹\,x=6-5=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1,y=2$ and $z=3.$

Question 4
?

Consider the system of linear equations {x+y+z=6y+z=52x+3y+2z=14 Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.

a
x=1,y=6 and z=−1
b
x=1,y=5 and z=0
c
x=1,y=2 and z=3
d
x=1,y=8 and z=−3
e
x=1,y=4 and z=1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is M=[1116011523214]. Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[1116011523214]R3:=R3−2R1∼[111601150102]R3:=R3+(−1)R2∼[1116011500−1−3]R3:=−R3∼[111601150013].

The system is now
{x+y+z=6y+z=5z=3,

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation z=3 tells us the value of z. Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

y+(3)=5⟹y=5−3=2.

Finally, substituting both y=2 and z=3 into the first equation, we get

x+(2)+(3)=6⟹x=6−5=1.

Therefore, the solution is x=1,y=2 and z=3.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & 2x+3y+2z=14\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=3$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(3)=5\,⟹\,y=5-3=2.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=2$ and $z=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(2)+(3)=6\,⟹\,x=6-5=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1,y=2$ and $z=3.$

Question 5
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[3−63−9−25−4403−52]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨5,6,4⟩
b
⟨−1,2,2⟩
c
⟨5,14,8⟩
d
⟨17,6,8⟩
e
⟨17,14,8⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/3, then R₂ ← R₂ + 2R₁, and R₃ ← R₃ − 3R₂. The row echelon matrix has rows [1,−2,1,−3], [0,1,−2,−2], and [0,0,1,8]. Back substitution gives z=8, y=14, and x=17, matching option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=-3 \\  & y-2z=-2 \\  & z=8,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=8$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-2(8)=-2\,⟹\,y=-2+16=14.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=14$ and $z=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(14)+(8)=-3\,⟹\,x=17.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=17,y=14$, and $z=8.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨17,14,8⟩.$

Question 5

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[3−63−9−25−4403−52]. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨5,6,4⟩
b
⟨−1,2,2⟩
c
⟨5,14,8⟩
d
⟨17,6,8⟩
e
⟨17,14,8⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[3−63−9−25−4403−52]R1:=13R1∼[1−21−3−25−4403−52]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−21−301−2−203−52]R3:=R3−3R2∼[1−21−301−2−20018].

The system is now
{x−2y+z=−3y−2z=−2z=8,

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation z=8 tells us the value of z. Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

y−2(8)=−2⟹y=−2+16=14.

Finally, substituting both y=14 and z=8 into the first equation, we get

x−2(14)+(8)=−3⟹x=17.

Therefore, the solution is x=17,y=14, and z=8. Or, in vector form, ⟨17,14,8⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=-3 \\  & y-2z=-2 \\  & z=8,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=8$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-2(8)=-2\,⟹\,y=-2+16=14.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=14$ and $z=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(14)+(8)=-3\,⟹\,x=17.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=17,y=14$, and $z=8.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨17,14,8⟩.$

before.name: Question 6
before.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

Consider the system of linear equations {x−y+2z=8−2x+2y−3z=−11x+z=9.

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
x=−1, y=2, and z=5
b
x=1, y=−6, and z=−5
c
x=4, y=6, and z=5
d
x=4, y=5, and z=2
e
x=4, y=−5, and z=2
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + 2R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − R₁, then swap R₂ and R₃. The row echelon matrix has rows [1,−1,2,8], [0,1,−1,1], and [0,0,1,5]. Back substitution gives z=5, y=6, and x=4, matching option c.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
x=−1, y=2, and z=5
b
x=1, y=−6, and z=−5
c
x=4, y=6, and z=5
d
x=4, y=5, and z=2

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The augmented matrix for this system is

M=[1−128−22−3−111019].

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[1−128−22−3−111019]R2:=R2+2R1∼[1−12800151019]R3:=R3+(−1)R1∼[1−128001501−11].

Note that we get a22=0. Therefore, we swap the 2nd and 3rd rows:

M∼[1−128001502−11]R2↔R3∼[1−12801−110015]

So, the system is now

{x−y+2z=8y−z=1z=5,

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation z=5 tells us the value of z. Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

y−(5)=1⟹y=6.

Now, substituting y=6 and z=5 into the first equation, we get

x−(6)+2(5)=8⟹x=4.

Thus, the solution is x=4, y=6, and z=5.

verification.explanation: Eliminating x and swapping the last two rows gives echelon rows [1,−1,2,8], [0,1,−1,1], and [0,0,1,5]. Thus z=5, y=6, and x=4. This confirms option c and satisfies all three original equations. The worked solution’s intermediate entry 2 in column two is a typo; it should be 1.

The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

Question 7
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[4−4−128−1110−503−9−6].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−14−20114−700137]
b
M∼[1−1−320132001−7]
c
M∼[1−1−3201−3−2001−37]
d
M∼[1−1−3201−3−2001−3]
e
M∼[1−1−4201−2−3001−37]
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₁ ← R₁/4, then R₂ ← R₂ + R₁, giving R₂ = [0,0,7,−3]. Swap R₂ and R₃, then divide the new R₂ by 3 and R₃ by 7. The resulting rows are [1,−1,−3,2], [0,1,−3,−2], and [0,0,1,−3/7], matching option c.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{7}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[4−4−128−1110−503−9−6].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−14−20114−700137]
b
M∼[1−1−320132001−7]
c
M∼[1−1−3201−3−2001−37]
d
M∼[1−1−3201−3−2001−3]
e
M∼[1−1−4201−2−3001−37]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[4−4−128−1110−503−9−6]R1:=14R1∼[1−1−32−1110−503−9−6]R2:=R2+R1∼[1−1−32007−303−9−6].

Note that we get a22=0. Therefore, we swap the 2nd and 3rd rows: M∼[1−1−32007−303−9−6]R2↔R3∼[1−1−3203−9−6007−3]

Finally, we multiply the 2nd row by 13 and the 3rd row by 17 to get M∼[1−1−3203−9−6007−3]R2:=13R2∼[1−1−3201−3−2007−3]R3:=17R3∼[1−1−3201−3−2001−37].

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{7}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[11−23−2−25−234−11].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨11,−8,0⟩
b
⟨−17,12,−4⟩
c
⟨25,−18,2⟩
d
⟨39,−28,4⟩
e
⟨−3,2,−2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Apply R₂ ← R₂ + 2R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − 3R₁, then swap R₂ and R₃. The echelon rows are [1,1,−2,3], [0,1,5,−8], and [0,0,1,4]. Back substitution gives z=4, y=−28, and x=39, matching option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

Question 8
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[11−23−2−25−234−11].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

a
⟨11,−8,0⟩
b
⟨−17,12,−4⟩
c
⟨25,−18,2⟩
d
⟨39,−28,4⟩
e
⟨−3,2,−2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have

M∼[11−23−2−25−234−11]R2:=R2+2R1∼[11−23001434−11]R3:=R3+(−3)R1∼[11−230014015−8].

Note that we get a22=0. Therefore, we swap the 2nd and 3rd rows:

M∼[11−230014015−8]R2↔R3∼[11−23015−80014]

So, the system is now

{x+y−2z=3y+5z=−8z=4,

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation z=4 tells us the value of z. Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

y+5(4)=−8⟹y=−28.

Now, substituting y=−28 and z=4 into the first equation, we get

x+(−28)−2(4)=3⟹x=39.

Thus, the solution is x=39, y=−28, and z=4. Or, in vector form ⟨39,−28,4⟩.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d. Applying R₂ ← R₂ + 2R₁ and R₃ ← R₃ − 3R₁, then swapping the last two rows, gives x+y−2z=3, y+5z=−8, and z=4. Back substitution yields y=−28 and x=39.

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
after.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=-2 \\ y+2z=-1 \\ z=11,\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
content.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=-2 \\ y+2z=-1 \\ z=11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=11$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(11)=-1\,⟹\,y=-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-23$ and $z=11$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-23)+3(11)=-2\,⟹\,x=-58.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-58$, $y=-23$, and $z=11.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-58,-23,11⟩.$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form.

a
M∼[1−21−201−230012]
b
M∼[1−21−201−230011]
c
M∼[1−21−201−210013]
d
M∼[1−21−201−420013]
e

decision.explanation: Divide R₁ by 3, then apply R₂ ← R₂ − 2R₁ to obtain [0,0,1,3]. Swap R₂ and R₃, then divide the new R₂ by 2. The echelon rows are [1,−2,1,−2], [0,1,−2,1], and [0,0,1,3], matching option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-6y+3z=-6 \\  & 2x-4y+3z=-1 \\  & 2y-4z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
after.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
content.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-6y+3z=-6 \\  & 2x-4y+3z=-1 \\  & 2y-4z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
content.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
